summary: Angeles NF lookout on Sierra Pelona Ridge; register dates it 1934 with a 30-foot tower, removal date unknown, only concrete slabs left and an OHV route reaches the site.

facts.design: California Region 5 BC-301 cabin atop a 30-foot K-brace steel tower
facts.status_note: Tower removed on a date no source gives; only a few concrete slabs remain (Angeles Adventures)

staffing.status: active into at least 1976 (register); several named staff 1938-1976

access.note: Reached by an off-road vehicle route on Angeles National Forest land; the sources read give no closure or permit rule

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Angeles National Forest

events.note: Register Built field; register text says constructed between 1934 and 1936
Windstorm forced the operator to evacuate; the register and a Star-News item both report it
Bee Canyon brush fire, about 10 acres, spotted from the lookout; about 175 firefighters
Ranger Casparis stationed in the tower (Valley News item quoted on Forest Lookouts)
Register: active as to at least 1976; Cal Bedient named as staff in 1976

evidence.supports: built 1934, constructed between 1934 and 1936 by the Angeles National Forest
evidence.quote: Sierra Pelona Lookout was constructed sometime between 1934 and 1936 by the Angeles National Forest.

evidence.supports: cab is a BC-301 design atop a 30-foot K-brace steel tower
evidence.quote: The structure is a California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin atop a 30 foot K-Brace steel tower.

evidence.supports: tower is a 30-foot steel K-brace tower
evidence.quote: Tower: Battered, open galvanized steel angle iron K-brace tower, 30ft

evidence.supports: lookout first appeared on a 1932 topo map
evidence.quote: The lookout first appeared on this Mint Canyon Topo Map from 1932.

evidence.supports: joined the Newhall District in 1932; tower given as 30-40 feet
evidence.quote: The tower measured at 30-40 feet tall and was part of the Newhall District beginning in 1932.

evidence.supports: a 1964 newspaper item describes a 40-foot tower
evidence.quote: who is stationed in a 40-foot tower on Sierra Pelona Lookout at the 4000-foot level

evidence.supports: named staff: Ross Lewis 1938, Ethel R. Babcock 1953, Cal Bedient 1976
evidence.quote: A few staff of the lookout included Ross Lewis in 1938, Irving Fritzen in 1949, Mrs. Ethel R. Babcock in 1953, Wilton A. Casparis in 1961, Claudia Wilson in 1974, and Cal Bedient in 1976.
Sierra Pelona was active as to at least 1976.

evidence.supports: 1956 windstorm forced the operator to evacuate
evidence.quote: A windstorm caused enough damage to the lookout to require an evacuation of the operator in 1956.

evidence.supports: a newspaper item said the tower was reportedly coming apart in the 1956 gale
evidence.quote: The lookout tower was reportedly disintegrating in the gale and the lookout was ordered to evacuate the structure.

evidence.supports: the 1964 Bee Canyon fire was spotted by the lookout
evidence.quote: The fire was spotted at 12:30 p.m. by a lookout in the Sierra Polona station

evidence.supports: about 175 firefighters worked the 1964 fire for nearly two hours
evidence.quote: Some 175 firemen battled the blaze in 100 degree temperatures for nearly two hours

evidence.supports: removal of the tower is unexplained and undated
evidence.quote: It is unclear why and when the tower was removed.

evidence.supports: newspaper articles place the lookout as still existing in the 1980s
evidence.quote: Newspaper articles place the lookout as still existing in the 1980s

evidence.supports: only a few concrete slabs remain at the site today
evidence.quote: Today only a few concrete slabs remain of the historic lookout.

evidence.supports: an OHV route leads directly to the site
evidence.quote: One of the numerous OHV routes leads directly to the site of the former lookout tower

evidence.supports: heavy gusts to 100 mph were frequently recorded at the site
evidence.quote: Heavy winds gusts to 100 mph were frequently recorded at Sierra Pelona.

evidence.supports: the Bee Canyon brush fire was on August 11, 1964

corrections.why: The register and Angeles Adventures both give a 30-foot tower. The 12.2 m (40 ft) figure matches only a 1964 newspaper description quoted by Forest Lookouts.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1934 and says construction ran from 1934 to 1936. Angeles Adventures says the lookout first appeared on a 1932 topo map and joined the Newhall District that year. The story reports both.

The register and Angeles Adventures' details block say 30 feet, though Angeles Adventures' text also says 30-40 feet; a 1964 newspaper item quoted on Forest Lookouts says 40 feet. The facts use 30 feet.

notes_for_editor: The record's 12.2 m height comes only from the 1964 newspaper item; the register and Angeles Adventures say 30 ft, so the facts use 9.1. Staff names come from Angeles Adventures, not the register. The Bee Canyon fire item (Valley News, quoted on Forest Lookouts) spells the station 'Sierra Polona'. No new photos added; the record already has six.
